title: RBAC v2 safety simulator and evidence replay notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the current thinking for a lightweight, reproducible RBAC v2 'safety simulator' that replays production audit events to validate permission model changes before broad rollout. Goal is to detect likely false-allow/false-deny regressions, generate SIEM-friendly evidence bundles, and provide deterministic rollback criteria for policy changes.

Background / Motivation:
- RBAC v2 introduces attribute-backed grants, timebound roles, and finer scoping. We need confidence that transformations (old->new) do not introduce security or availability regressions.
- Existing approaches (static review, unit tests) miss emergent access patterns visible only in production traffic.
- A simulator that replays historical events against candidate policy trees gives us quantitative signals and reproducible artifacts for audits and SOC review.

Scope & non-goals:
- IN SCOPE: replay of past audit log events, mapping of legacy entitlements to RBAC v2 model, comparators that classify outcome deltas, automated evidence bundle generation, SIEM export adapter to test forward compatibility.
- OUT OF SCOPE: live enforcement changes, full drift remediation automation, privilege revocation workflows (these are downstream).

High-level architecture (conceptual):
1) Event extractor: sample/stream of audit events (S3 snapshot, Kafka topic).
2) Normalizer: canonicalize fields to 'simulation schema' (see below), mask PII, preserve request_id/session_id ordering.
3) Policy transpiler: compiles candidate RBAC v2 rules into a deterministic decision graph (sim-only runtime).
4) Replayer/Simulator: deterministic runner that evaluates each event against baseline policy and candidate policy; records outcome and context.
5) Evidence packer: for any divergence of interest, produce a signed evidence bundle (JSONL + minimal raw request excerpts) for SIEM ingest and compliance review.
6) Metrics/QA service: summary metrics, alerts, and automatic ticket creation when thresholds exceeded.
7) SIEM adapter: converts evidence bundles to the SIEM export schema and attempts a dry-run ingest to the SIEM staging pipeline.

Simulation data schema (fields we need preserved):
- timestamp (ISO8601 string)
- event_type (string: api_call, console_action, token_issue, etc.)
- actor_id (string)
- actor_role_snapshot (string)
- target_resource (string)
- action (string)
- outcome (string: allow|deny|error)
- request_id (string)
- session_id (string)
- raw_request_snippet (string, masked)
- policy_revision (string)
- location/region (string)
- keystones (list of strings) -- list serialized as CSV in-line for compatibility with existing logs
- original_log_id (string)

Mapping to SIEM export: we propose the following fields map for SIEM dry-run
- siem.timestamp <- timestamp
- siem.actor <- actor_id
- siem.resource <- target_resource
- siem.verb <- action
- siem.result <- outcome (normalize to success/failure with codes)
- siem.evidence_bundle_id <- generated bundle id
- siem.policy_delta <- short summary (allow->deny / deny->allow)
- siem.raw_snippet <- raw_request_snippet (if allowed by privacy rules)

Simulation scenarios to run:
- Full-pass: replay entire 30-day window at 1% sampling to get population metrics.
- Focused cohorts: high-impact resources (billing, key-management, deploy), 100% replay for last 7 days.
- Timebound role test: evaluate behavior of time-limited grants around boundary times.
- Lateral-movement check: sequences where actor performs cross-resource actions in short windows.
- Escalation sequence detect: simulation looks for events where a deny in baseline but allow in candidate occurs followed by a sensitive action thereafter.

Metrics & thresholds (initial):
- false_allow_rate: candidate_allow && baseline_deny events / total_events_sampled. Alert at > 0.01% for critical resources, > 0.1% for non-critical.
- false_deny_rate: candidate_deny && baseline_allow events / total_events_sampled. Alert at > 0.5% overall or if any customer-facing route affected.
- evidence_coverage_pct: percent of divergence events with valid evidence bundle; target > 95%.
- simulation_latency_p50/p95 (per-100k events) for ops sizing.

Acceptance criteria for a policy change to progress out of canary: all thresholds below alert levels for two independent windows (7d sample, and focused cohort run).

Test plan & sampling heuristics:
- Dataset selection: retain last 90 days of audit events in cold storage. For initial runs, use 30-day rolling window.
- Sampling: stratified by resource criticality and actor churn. Maintain reservoir sampling to preserve long-tail sessions.
- Determinism: seed replayer RNG and persist seed with run metadata so runs are replayable for postmortem.

Evidence bundle format (single-file JSONL manifest + gzipped raw snippets):
- bundle_id (uuid)
content_2:
- manifest.jsonl entries: {event_hash, timestamp, actor_id, target_resource, action, baseline_outcome, candidate_outcome, diff_class, attached_snippet_key}
- attached_snippet_key indexes into gzipped object store; snippets are redacted and HMAC-signed.
- bundle signed with internal evidence key; include signature metadata for SOC ingestion.

Runbook (playtest run):
1) Checkout candidate ruleset (git tag) and compile via policy transpiler. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-sim/pull/78
2) Provision ephemeral replayer infra (k8s job, 4 replicas for sampling).
3) Run normalization against S3 snapshot: s3://rbac-audit-archive/2024/11/01-30
4) Execute full-pass 1% sample; record metrics to metrics cluster.
5) Execute focused cohort for critical resources (billing, kms, deploy) at 100%.
6) Collect divergence set, generate evidence bundles, run SIEM dry-run.
7) Triage divergences with triage owners (see linked tickets).
8) If false_allow_rate > threshold for critical resources: abort rollout, open incident, and schedule emergency rollback timeline.

Rollout plan (staged):
- Stage 0: simulation-only (no enforcement) — run weekly and after each major policy change.
- Stage 1: advisory mode in non-prod (policy denies logged but not enforced). 0% enforcement.
- Stage 2: canary enforcement on 1% of sessions (non-customer-facing namespaces). Monitor 48h.
- Stage 3: expand to 10% with automated rollback if any critical false_allow observed.
- Stage 4: full rollout with monitoring and quarterly audits.

Automated rollback criteria (examples):
- Any critical-resource false_allow > 0 events within canary window.
- Increase in customer-facing false_deny causing 5+ customer incidents in 24h.
- Evidence coverage below 90% for divergence events.

Alerting & ownership:
- PagerDuty: security-oncall (primary), infra-sre (secondary).
- Slack escalation channel: #rbac-sim-alerts (hooked to runbook bot).
- Ticketing: auto-create SEC- tickets when thresholds crossed; link to multiplexed evidence bundles.

Privacy & compliance guardrails:
- Raw snippets should be redacted: only include request shapes and truncated PII-free payload summaries.
- Access to evidence bundles requires additional approval scope and audit trail.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What retention policy for simulation runs and evidence bundles (30/90/365 days)?
- How to seed policy transpiler with transient attributes (tokens linked to ephemeral grants)?
- SIEM staging: can we provide a dedicated staging index and test account? (see SEC-4312)

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Aisha: prototype normalizer for 30-day snapshot (prototype due 2025-01-10) -> ticket SEC-4389
- Jonah: implement deterministic seed storage and runner metadata logging -> PR #82
- Priya: draft SIEM dry-run mapping and request staging credentials from SOC -> CON-2047
- Marcus: build evidence bundle signer and storage layout; coordinate key rotation with security ops.

Appendix: quick sample divergence entry (redacted)
{
  timestamp: "2025-02-08T14:12:03Z",
  event_type: "api_call",
  actor_id: "user:u-12345",
  target_resource: "projects/infra/secrets/key-33",
  action: "read_secret",
  baseline_outcome: "deny",
  candidate_outcome: "allow",
  diff_class: "critical-false-allow",
  evidence_bundle_id: "bundle-20250208-7a2f"
}

Notes / informal observations from initial playtest runs:
- Many false_denies are from stale service-accounts that had temporary grants. We should surface expiration metadata in transpiler.
- Lateral sequence detector flagged ~12 sessions that need deeper session stitching logic.

If you are reviewing: please add comments inline, and ping on Slack for any blockers. Will iterate this doc into a more formal playbook once we validate the prototype.
